enforced_dimensions.max_input_bytes: codec/reader/reader.py -- enforced on both path.stat().st_size (before reading) and len(data) for bytes/stream sources, with the stream read itself bounded to limits.max_input_bytes + 1 so an oversized stream is never fully buffered before the check fires
enforced_dimensions.max_xml_nodes: codec/reader/reader.py -- enforced incrementally during element parsing, not only after full materialization
enforced_dimensions.max_nesting_depth: codec/reader/reader.py -- enforced incrementally during element parsing
enforced_dimensions.max_entries: codec/reader/reader.py -- enforced per-element on attribute_count (an attribute flood on a single element is rejected even if total node/depth limits are not exceeded)
enforced_dimensions.max_decompressed_bytes: codec/reader/reader.py -- enforced on cumulative decoded text_bytes across the document
enforced_dimensions.max_output_bytes: codec/writer/writer.py -- enforced on the final encoded byte length

evidence.key_proof: test_node_and_depth_limits_are_enforced and test_a_wide_sibling_flood_is_rejected_by_node_count_not_depth together prove max_xml_nodes and max_nesting_depth are independent dimensions (a wide-but-shallow tree is bounded by node count, not depth); test_an_attribute_flood_on_one_element_is_rejected proves max_entries is a per-element guard, not merely a whole-document total.

honest_gap: max_input_bytes, max_decompressed_bytes, and max_output_bytes are enforced in the source (confirmed by direct code inspection, cited above) but do not currently have their own dedicated named test in the same style as the node/depth/entries tests -- an honest disclosure, not a hidden gap. The enforcement itself is real and exercised incidentally by the broader test suite's own many load/dump round-trips, which would fail if these guards were absent or broken, but a dedicated positive/negative pair for each (matching the depth of coverage the other 3 dimensions have) was not added this tick.
